title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 1 questions (1.1, 1.2, 1.3)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A company is building its first identity model in a new Identity Security Cloud tenant, with Workday as the HR system. What should the engineer do FIRST?
choices: Create the lifecycle states that HR asked for in the design workshop
Build department roles so new identities receive access right away
Aggregate Active Directory so its accounts are ready to correlate later
Configure and test the Workday source, then aggregate its accounts
questions.answer: Configure and test the Workday source, then aggregate its accounts
questions.explanation: An identity profile is built on an existing source, so the HR source must be connected and aggregated first. Roles and lifecycle states depend on identities and attributes that do not exist yet.

questions.stem: An engineer has created an identity profile for the HR source and mapped its identity attributes. What should the engineer do before selecting Apply Changes?
choices: Preview several identities to confirm the mapped values
Run an entitlement aggregation on the HR source to refresh its schema
Enable every lifecycle state so identities are assigned during processing
Reset the HR source so its accounts are aggregated again from scratch
questions.answer: Preview several identities to confirm the mapped values
questions.explanation: Preview shows the calculated attribute values for real identities before processing runs across the profile. Resetting or re-aggregating the source adds nothing and enabling unfinished lifecycle states could trigger provisioning.

questions.stem: A consultant recommends onboarding the HR source as authoritative before connecting Active Directory and other target sources. What is the main reason for this order?
choices: Target sources cannot be created in a tenant that has no identity profile
Active Directory accounts are deleted when no identity profile exists yet
Other accounts correlate to identities, so identities must exist first
Aggregation of other sources stays blocked until lifecycle states are enabled
questions.answer: Other accounts correlate to identities, so identities must exist first
questions.explanation: Non-authoritative accounts are matched to existing identities by correlation, so building identities first avoids a large set of uncorrelated accounts. Target sources can be created at any time; their accounts would simply remain uncorrelated.

questions.stem: An engineer tries to create an identity profile for a new HR source while that source's account aggregation is still running. What should the engineer do?
choices: Remove the source's correlation configuration and try again
Wait for the aggregation to finish, then create the identity profile
Create the profile on another source and switch it to HR later
Run identity processing on another profile so the aggregation stops early
questions.answer: Wait for the aggregation to finish, then create the identity profile
questions.explanation: An identity profile cannot be created while an account aggregation is running on the tenant, so the engineer waits for it to complete. Changing correlation or using another source does not lift that restriction.

questions.stem: During design workshops for a new identity model, which activity should be completed before any identity profile is configured?
choices: Configure approval reminders and escalation chains for every requestable item
Build manager certification campaigns for every department
Create access request segments for each business unit
Agree with HR on the system of record and attributes for each population
questions.answer: Agree with HR on the system of record and attributes for each population
questions.explanation: Identity profiles depend on knowing each population's authoritative source and its attributes. Reminders, certifications and segments are later governance layers that rely on the identity model being in place.

questions.stem: Before the first aggregation of a new HR source, which source setting should the engineer verify so identity attributes can be mapped from complete data?
choices: The source is selected as the sign-in source for all users
The account schema includes every HR attribute the mappings will use
Every access profile on the source is marked as requestable
Attribute sync is enabled for each identity attribute that the source supports
questions.answer: The account schema includes every HR attribute the mappings will use
questions.explanation: Mappings can only use attributes that the account schema brings in during aggregation, so missing schema attributes leave identity attributes empty. Pass-through sign-in, requestable access profiles and attribute sync do not affect what is read from HR.

questions.stem: An engineer has connected and aggregated the HR source. Which step turns the HR accounts into identities?
choices: Running a second account aggregation with the correlation configuration turned on
Adding the HR accounts to a governance group for approval
Creating an identity profile that uses the HR source and processing it
Enabling attribute sync for the HR source's account attributes
questions.answer: Creating an identity profile that uses the HR source and processing it
questions.explanation: A source becomes authoritative when an identity profile is configured for it, and processing that profile creates an identity for each account. Aggregation alone only loads accounts.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes what makes a source authoritative in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: An identity profile is configured with that source as its source
It is the first source that was aggregated in the tenant
It is connected through a virtual appliance cluster
It contains the largest number of accounts in the tenant
questions.answer: An identity profile is configured with that source as its source
questions.explanation: A source becomes authoritative when an identity profile is built on it, and an identity is created for each of its accounts. Aggregation order, connection method and account volume do not make a source authoritative.

questions.stem: An architect proposes making Active Directory the authoritative source for every user because all staff have an AD account. What is the MAIN concern with this design?
choices: Identity Security Cloud cannot read AD attributes through a virtual appliance
AD accounts cannot be correlated to identities once aggregated
AD sources are unable to provide work email addresses
Service, test and shared AD accounts would also become identities
questions.answer: Service, test and shared AD accounts would also become identities
questions.explanation: Every account on an authoritative source becomes an identity, so non-human AD accounts would pollute the identity model. AD is normally a target source whose accounts correlate to identities from HR.

questions.stem: Interns are already in Workday, which backs the Employees identity profile. An engineer wants a second identity profile on the same Workday source so interns get different lifecycle states. What is the problem with this plan?
choices: Interns cannot be loaded from a source that also holds employees
A source can be the authoritative source for only one identity profile
A second profile would need a separate virtual appliance cluster
Lifecycle states can only be created in the first identity profile of a tenant
questions.answer: A source can be the authoritative source for only one identity profile
questions.explanation: Each source can back only one identity profile, so interns from Workday stay in the Employees profile. Their differences are handled with identity attributes such as worker type and the lifecycle state calculation.

questions.stem: Which characteristic MOST qualifies a source to be the authoritative source for a population?
choices: It is the system of record for that population, with start and end dates
It is the application that holds the largest number of entitlements
It supports password changes and account unlocks for users
It can be reached directly from the cloud without needing a virtual appliance
questions.answer: It is the system of record for that population, with start and end dates
questions.explanation: An authoritative source should be the trusted record of who is in the population and when they join and leave. Entitlement volume, password features and connection type say nothing about whether its people data is trustworthy.

questions.stem: Contractors exist only as accounts that IT creates by hand in Active Directory, and there is no contractor feed. The client wants contractors governed by lifecycle states. What is the BEST recommendation?
choices: Make Active Directory authoritative so that every AD account becomes an identity
Ask HR to enter the contractors in Workday as regular employees
Make a dedicated contractor source, such as a non-employee source, authoritative
Correlate the contractor AD accounts to the Employees identity profile
questions.answer: Make a dedicated contractor source, such as a non-employee source, authoritative
questions.explanation: A dedicated contractor system of record gives contractors their own identity profile, start and end dates and lifecycle states. AD as authoritative would create identities for every AD account, and correlation alone never creates identities.

questions.stem: Board members need identities, but they are not in the HR system. Legal keeps an accurate spreadsheet of current board members with their start and end dates. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Add the board members to the HR identity profile as manual identities
Create the board members as accounts on Active Directory and correlate them
Map the spreadsheet columns into the HR profile as extra identity attributes
Onboard the spreadsheet as a delimited file source with its own profile
questions.answer: Onboard the spreadsheet as a delimited file source with its own profile
questions.explanation: A delimited file source can be authoritative for a small population when it is the trusted record. Correlating to AD or mapping attributes into the HR profile does not create identities for people missing from HR.

questions.stem: Employees come from Workday. Contractors are tracked in a separate contractor management system that will be onboarded as its own source. How many identity profiles does the design need?
choices: Two identity profiles, one for each authoritative source
One identity profile, with contractor attributes mapped from the second source
Three identity profiles, one per source plus a shared profile for both groups
One identity profile for each department found in either source
questions.answer: Two identity profiles, one for each authoritative source
questions.explanation: Each authoritative source needs its own identity profile, so two populations from two systems of record means two profiles. A single profile can map attributes from other sources but has only one authoritative source.

questions.stem: Workday holds both employees and contingent workers, with a worker type attribute that tells them apart. Each group needs different birthright access. How many identity profiles should the engineer create?
choices: Two identity profiles on Workday, one for each worker type
One profile for Workday, with worker type driving access
One identity profile per worker type, each on a copy of the Workday source
Two identity profiles, with contingent workers loaded from Active Directory
questions.answer: One profile for Workday, with worker type driving access
questions.explanation: Both groups come from one authoritative source, so one profile is needed and the worker type attribute drives roles or lifecycle logic. Copying the HR source just to split a population adds aggregation load and maintenance for no benefit.

questions.stem: After an acquisition the company has three HR systems (Workday for the US, SAP SuccessFactors for Europe and a CSV feed for Latin America) and one contractor source. Each holds a separate population. How many identity profiles does the design need?
choices: One identity profile that maps attributes from all four sources
Two identity profiles, one for employees and one for contractors
Four identity profiles, one for each authoritative source
Three identity profiles, because the contractor source is not authoritative
questions.answer: Four identity profiles, one for each authoritative source
questions.explanation: Every source whose people should become identities needs its own identity profile. One profile cannot have several authoritative sources, so grouping by employee type is not possible across different systems.

questions.stem: A design document proposes one identity profile per department, all built on the single HR source. What is wrong with this design?
choices: A tenant is limited to two identity profiles in total
Department values cannot be mapped to identity attributes
Identity profiles must be created separately for each virtual appliance cluster
Each source backs only one identity profile, so one HR source means one profile
questions.answer: Each source backs only one identity profile, so one HR source means one profile
questions.explanation: One source can back only one identity profile, so department differences belong in identity attributes, roles and lifecycle logic. There is no two-profile limit and department is a default identity attribute.

questions.stem: Two staffing vendors each send a contractor file with the same columns, and the business requirements for both vendors' contractors are identical. Which design MINIMIZES the number of identity profiles while meeting the requirements?
choices: Combine both vendor files into one contractor source and one profile
Create one identity profile per vendor file and copy the mappings between them
Load both vendor files into the employee HR identity profile
Create no identity profile and correlate vendor rows to AD accounts
questions.answer: Combine both vendor files into one contractor source and one profile
questions.explanation: With identical requirements, a single combined contractor source needs only one identity profile, plus a vendor attribute if reporting needs it. Two vendor sources would require two profiles because each source backs one profile.

questions.stem: Employees come from Workday and contractors from a contractor source, and some contractors later become employees. How many identity profiles are needed and what else must be designed?
choices: One profile, with contractor accounts correlated into Workday
Two profiles with equal priority so attributes are merged
Two profiles, with Employees set to a higher priority than Contractors
Three profiles, adding a separate identity profile just for converted contractors
questions.answer: Two profiles, with Employees set to a higher priority than Contractors
questions.explanation: Two authoritative sources need two profiles, and priority decides which profile an identity with accounts on both uses. Profiles cannot share equal priority to merge data, and a third profile would need a third source.

questions.stem: An engineer created the Contractors identity profile before the Employees profile. Contractors who become employees keep their contractor attributes and lifecycle states. What is the cause?
choices: Employees has a lower priority number than Contractors
Contractors was created first, so it holds the higher priority
Converted identities must be deleted before they can change profile
Identity profiles share mappings, so the first profile's values win
questions.answer: Contractors was created first, so it holds the higher priority
questions.explanation: By default the earliest profile receives the highest priority, so an identity with accounts on both sources stays with Contractors. The fix is to give Employees a lower priority number than Contractors.

questions.stem: Two identity profiles have priority values of 10 and 20. Which statement is correct?
choices: The profile with priority 20 has the higher priority
The profile with priority 10 has the higher priority
Both profiles are equal until a tie-breaker rule is added
Priority only affects the order in which profiles are listed
questions.answer: The profile with priority 10 has the higher priority
questions.explanation: A lower priority number means a higher priority, and the first profile created gets 10 by default. Priority decides which profile an identity with accounts on several authoritative sources belongs to.

questions.stem: Which is the supported way for an engineer to change the priority order of existing identity profiles?
choices: Update each profile's priority value with the identity profile API
Re-aggregate the authoritative sources in the desired order
Change the order of the sources on the Sources page
Edit a priority field on each profile's Mappings page
questions.answer: Update each profile's priority value with the identity profile API
questions.explanation: Profile priority is set by creation order and changed by updating the priority attribute through the identity profile API. Aggregation order and the source list do not affect profile priority.

questions.stem: An identity has an account on the Workday source, whose profile has priority 10, and on the contractor source, whose profile has priority 20. Which profile's mappings populate the identity's attributes?
choices: The contractor profile, because its priority number is the larger one
Both profiles, merged attribute by attribute
The Workday profile, because it has the higher priority
Whichever source was aggregated most recently
questions.answer: The Workday profile, because it has the higher priority
questions.explanation: An identity belongs to only one identity profile: the highest priority one where it has an authoritative account. Attributes are never merged across profiles, and aggregation timing does not change the association.

questions.stem: An employee who was also a contractor leaves, and HR removes the Workday record. The person's contractor account is still on the contractor source. What happens to the identity?
choices: It is deleted along with all of its correlated accounts
It keeps the Employees profile until an admin moves it
It stays in the Employees profile with frozen attribute values
It moves to the contractor profile, whose mappings then apply
questions.answer: It moves to the contractor profile, whose mappings then apply
questions.explanation: When the higher priority authoritative account disappears but another authoritative account remains, the identity is associated with the next profile where it has an account. Only an identity with no remaining authoritative account is removed.

questions.stem: Identities can move between the Employees and Contractors profiles. Why should the lifecycle state technical names be planned for both profiles together?
choices: Lifecycle states are shared across the tenant, so names in one profile overwrite the other
Only the highest priority profile is allowed to define lifecycle states
States are per profile, so the value must match a state in the identity's new profile
Technical names must differ between profiles or processing fails
questions.answer: States are per profile, so the value must match a state in the identity's new profile
questions.explanation: Each profile has its own lifecycle states, and an identity whose cloudLifecycleState value has no matching state in its profile shows a not-valid status. Coordinated names keep moves between profiles predictable.

questions.stem: A design has three authoritative sources: Employees, Contingent Workers and Alumni. Some people appear in all three. Which priority order BEST reflects their trust level?
choices: Alumni highest, because those records are the oldest
Employees highest, then Contingent Workers, then Alumni
Contingent Workers highest, because they change most often
All three with the same priority so the newest record wins
questions.answer: Employees highest, then Contingent Workers, then Alumni
questions.explanation: The most trusted and current relationship should win, so active employment ranks first and alumni records last. Two profiles cannot share a priority to let the newest record win.

questions.stem: After the first aggregation, the HR identity profile shows identity exceptions for accounts that have no last name. What should the engineer do?
choices: Delete the identity profile and create it again on the same HR source afterwards
Remove Last Name from the required attributes in the profile
Correlate the accounts manually to existing identities
Download the exceptions report, fix the records in HR and aggregate again
questions.answer: Download the exceptions report, fix the records in HR and aggregate again
questions.explanation: Identity exceptions mean required values such as Last Name are missing, and they are resolved by correcting the source data and aggregating again. Last Name cannot be made optional and recreating the profile changes nothing.

questions.stem: Two HR records produce the same User Name value after mapping. What is the result?
choices: An identity exception, because User Name must be unique
Both identities are created and the second gets a numeric suffix
The second record is merged into the first identity
The older identity is deleted and replaced by the newer one
questions.answer: An identity exception, because User Name must be unique
questions.explanation: User Name (uid) must be unique across every identity profile, and a duplicate generates an identity exception. ISC does not add suffixes or merge identities on its own; a transform can make the value unique.

questions.stem: An engineer changed a mapping on the Employees profile yesterday, but identities still show the old values and the profile status reads Needs Processing. What should the engineer do?
choices: Select Apply Changes so identity processing runs for the profile
Run an entitlement aggregation on every connected source
Recreate the lifecycle states so the new mapping is used
Reset the HR source to clear its cached account data
questions.answer: Select Apply Changes so identity processing runs for the profile
questions.explanation: Saved mapping changes take effect when identity processing runs, which Apply Changes starts for that profile. Entitlement aggregation and source resets do not recalculate identity attributes.

questions.stem: HR updates an employee's department in Workday, and the next scheduled aggregation of Workday loads the change. What happens to the identity?
choices: Nothing changes until an admin selects Apply Changes on the profile
The identity is recreated with a new identity ID
Its attributes are reprocessed automatically after the aggregation
The change waits until the next certification campaign starts
questions.answer: Its attributes are reprocessed automatically after the aggregation
questions.explanation: ISC automatically processes identity data that changes during aggregation, so the department updates without manual steps. Apply Changes is needed for configuration changes, not for normal data changes.

questions.stem: An engineer deletes an old identity profile. Its identities have no account on any other authoritative source. What is the result?
choices: The source and all of its accounts are deleted from the tenant
The identities are deleted and their source accounts become uncorrelated
The identities' accounts are deprovisioned from every connected target system
The identities remain in the tenant without any identity profile
questions.answer: The identities are deleted and their source accounts become uncorrelated
questions.explanation: Deleting a profile makes its source non-authoritative and deletes identities that cannot move to another profile, leaving their accounts uncorrelated. It does not delete the source or deprovision accounts in target systems.

questions.stem: No aggregation is running, but an engineer cannot delete an old identity profile. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The profile still has lifecycle states defined
The profile's source has entitlements loaded
The profile has the highest priority in the tenant
Some of the profile's identities are still source or app owners
questions.answer: Some of the profile's identities are still source or app owners
questions.explanation: Identities that own sources or apps block deletion of their profile until ownership is reassigned. Lifecycle states, entitlements and priority do not prevent deletion.

questions.stem: A helpdesk analyst notices several identities flagged as Incomplete on the Identities page. What does this MOST likely indicate?
choices: They have not been certified in the last campaign
They are missing required values such as User Name, Work Email or Last Name
They have no accounts on any non-authoritative source
Their lifecycle state is set to a disabled state
questions.answer: They are missing required values such as User Name, Work Email or Last Name
questions.explanation: Identities missing required attributes show as Incomplete and also appear as identity exceptions. Certification status, target accounts and lifecycle state do not mark an identity incomplete.

questions.stem: An engineer is implementing the identity model for a new Workday HR source. Put the steps in order.
items: Configure the Workday source and test the connection
Create an identity profile with Workday as its source
Map the required and custom identity attributes
Preview identities to check the mapped values
Apply changes to process the profile's identities
questions.explanation: The source and its accounts must exist before a profile can be built on them, mappings are verified with Preview, and Apply Changes then processes the identities.

questions.stem: Employees come from Workday and contractors from a contractor source. Some contractors later become employees and keep both accounts for a while. Which TWO statements describe the correct design?
choices: Create two identity profiles, one for each source
Give the Employees profile a lower priority number than Contractors
Create one identity profile and map contractor data into it
Give both profiles the same priority so attributes are merged
Make Active Directory authoritative for both groups
answers: Create two identity profiles, one for each source
Give the Employees profile a lower priority number than Contractors
questions.explanation: Each authoritative source needs its own profile, and a lower priority number gives Employees precedence for people with accounts on both. Attributes are never merged across profiles.

questions.stem: Employees come from Workday, but their work email address is only stored in Active Directory. How should the engineer populate the Work Email identity attribute for the Employees profile?
choices: Add Active Directory as a second authoritative source of the same profile
Create a second identity profile on Active Directory that supplies email
Map Work Email in the Employees profile to the AD mail account attribute
Use attribute sync to copy the AD mail value into Workday first
questions.answer: Map Work Email in the Employees profile to the AD mail account attribute
questions.explanation: Identity attributes can be mapped from account attributes on any source, so the Workday profile can take email from AD. A profile has only one authoritative source, and attribute sync pushes values out to targets rather than feeding mappings.

questions.stem: The Contractors profile should take department from the contractor source, while the Employees profile takes it from Workday. How should the engineer configure this?
choices: Create a second department attribute used only by contractors
Map department once, because mappings are shared by all profiles
Use a rule that checks the profile name before choosing a source
Map the department attribute separately in each identity profile
questions.answer: Map the department attribute separately in each identity profile
questions.explanation: Mappings are defined per identity profile, so the same attribute can come from a different source in each one. A second attribute or a rule adds complexity for something mappings already support.

questions.stem: Users with international phone numbers cannot use them for verification. Which mapping change addresses this?
choices: Apply the ISO3166 Country Format transform to the Work Phone attribute
Apply the E.164 Phone Format transform to the Work Phone attribute
Map Work Phone from Active Directory instead of from HR
Apply the ToUpper transform to the Work Phone attribute
questions.answer: Apply the E.164 Phone Format transform to the Work Phone attribute
questions.explanation: International phone numbers require the Work Phone attribute to be in E.164 format, which the built-in simple transform provides. The ISO3166 transform formats country names, not phone numbers.

questions.stem: The HR attribute locations is multi-valued. After the engineer adds a ToUpper transform to its mapping, identities show only one location. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: A mapping transform on a multi-valued attribute uses only the first value
ToUpper removes duplicate values before returning a result
Identity attributes never accept values that are longer than a single word
The HR source only returns one value per aggregation
questions.answer: A mapping transform on a multi-valued attribute uses only the first value
questions.explanation: When a multi-valued attribute is passed through a mapping transform, only the first value is transformed into a single value. The other options describe behaviour ISC does not have.

questions.stem: Some users cannot sign in to the tenant, and all of them have usernames that contain an exclamation mark. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Exclamation marks are removed from usernames during aggregation
The users' passwords were reset when identity processing last ran
The mapped User Name contains characters not allowed for sign-in
Usernames must match the users' email address to sign in
questions.answer: The mapped User Name contains characters not allowed for sign-in
questions.explanation: Characters such as * ( ) & ! and the period are not allowed in the source attribute mapped to a username or alternative sign-in attribute, and affected users may not be able to sign in. ISC does not strip the characters for them.

questions.stem: Contractor identities should no longer receive a costCenter value, but employees still need it. What should the engineer do?
choices: Delete the costCenter attribute from the Contractors profile
Set the mapping's source to None in the Contractors profile and apply changes
Map costCenter in the Contractors profile to an empty static value from the HR source
Remove the costCenter column from the employee HR source schema
questions.answer: Set the mapping's source to None in the Contractors profile and apply changes
questions.explanation: Choosing None unmaps the attribute for that profile only. Deleting an identity attribute removes it from every profile, and costCenter is a default attribute that should not be deleted.

questions.stem: The Employees profile maps email from Active Directory, but new hires are aggregated from HR days before their AD account exists. What is the BEST mapping design?
choices: Map email from HR personal email for all employees
Wait to aggregate HR until every new hire's AD account has been created by the IT team
Leave email unmapped until the employee's start date
Use a firstValid transform that tries the AD mail value, then a fallback value
questions.answer: Use a firstValid transform that tries the AD mail value, then a fallback value
questions.explanation: firstValid returns the first non-null value in its list, so identities get a fallback until the AD mail attribute exists. Email is required and cannot stay unmapped, and delaying HR aggregation breaks the joiner process.

questions.stem: Which identity attributes must be mapped in every identity profile and cannot be null for any identity?
choices: User Name, Work Email and Last Name
User Name, Manager and Lifecycle State
First Name, Last Name and Department
Display Name, Work Email and Start Date
questions.answer: User Name, Work Email and Last Name
questions.explanation: User Name (uid), Work Email (email) and Last Name (lastname) are the required identity attributes. Manager and Lifecycle State are needed only for features that use them.

questions.stem: Some HR records have no work email yet because email accounts are created later. Which design prevents identity exceptions for these records?
choices: Removing Work Email from the list of required attributes
Mapping Work Email to the employee's manager's email
Creating a separate identity profile for all of the records that have no email
A transform that falls back to a placeholder value until the real email exists
questions.answer: A transform that falls back to a placeholder value until the real email exists
questions.explanation: Work Email cannot be null but is not validated as an address, so a firstValid style fallback keeps the identity complete until the real value arrives. Required attributes cannot be made optional.

questions.stem: The Employees and Contractors profiles both map User Name from a numeric ID, and the two systems reuse the same number ranges. What is the risk, and how should the engineer address it?
choices: Identities merge across profiles, so contractor IDs should be hidden from mappings
Each profile keeps its own namespace, so no change is needed
Duplicate user names cause exceptions, so prefix contractor IDs with a transform
Numeric user names are rejected, so names must be used instead
questions.answer: Duplicate user names cause exceptions, so prefix contractor IDs with a transform
questions.explanation: User Name must be unique across all identities from any identity profile, so overlapping IDs generate exceptions. A transform that adds a prefix or suffix keeps contractor values distinct.

questions.stem: An engineer maps Work Email to an HR field that sometimes holds the text N/A. How will Identity Security Cloud treat this value?
choices: It rejects the identity and creates a duplicate User Name exception
It accepts it, because Work Email is required but not validated as an address
It replaces the value with the user's Active Directory email automatically
It sends the value to SailPoint for review before saving it
questions.answer: It accepts it, because Work Email is required but not validated as an address
questions.explanation: Work Email cannot be null, but its format is not validated, so the value is stored as is. The engineer should clean the data or use a transform rather than expect ISC to correct it.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to remove the default initials identity attribute because the company never uses it. What is the BEST action?
choices: Leave the attribute unmapped rather than deleting it
Delete it from the Mappings page and apply changes
Map it to a static blank value in every profile
Rename it to a custom attribute the company uses
questions.answer: Leave the attribute unmapped rather than deleting it
questions.explanation: Default identity attributes should not be deleted; SailPoint Support must be contacted for that. Leaving an attribute unmapped has no side effects.

questions.stem: Beyond the required attributes, what must be in place for manager-based access request approvals to route correctly?
choices: A governance group named Managers for each department
A custom identity attribute holding each manager's email address for routing
A lifecycle state that grants a manager access profile
Manager Name mapped in the profile and manager correlation on a source
questions.answer: Manager Name mapped in the profile and manager correlation on a source
questions.explanation: Manager-based features need the Manager Name attribute mapped and a manager correlation configuration that links each identity to its manager. Governance groups and email attributes do not create the manager relationship.

questions.stem: An engineer has configured manager correlation on the HR source, but no identity shows a manager. The source settings are correct. What else is required?
choices: The Manager Name attribute must be mapped in each identity profile
Each manager must be added to a governance group
The HR source must be marked as an authentication source
A manager certification campaign must be completed
questions.answer: The Manager Name attribute must be mapped in each identity profile
questions.explanation: Manager correlation needs both a manager correlation configuration on the source and the Manager Name attribute mapped in each identity profile. Governance groups and certifications play no part in it.

questions.stem: The HR attribute managerEmployeeId holds each manager's employee number, which is mapped to the identificationNumber identity attribute. How should the Manager Correlation section be configured?
choices: Identity Attribute managerEmployeeId and Account Attribute identificationNumber
Identity Attribute identificationNumber and Account Attribute managerEmployeeId
Identity Attribute manager and Account Attribute managerEmployeeId
Identity Attribute uid and Account Attribute identificationNumber
questions.answer: Identity Attribute identificationNumber and Account Attribute managerEmployeeId
questions.explanation: The Identity Attribute is the value examined on the manager's identity, and the Account Attribute is the employee's account attribute that names the manager. Swapping them compares the wrong data.

questions.stem: Where does an engineer define the manager correlation configuration for an HR source?
choices: On the identity profile's Mappings page, under the Manager Name identity attribute
In the global system settings, under identity correlation options
In the source's Account Correlation settings, in the Manager Correlation section
On the source's Provisioning page, in the Create Account policy
questions.answer: In the source's Account Correlation settings, in the Manager Correlation section
questions.explanation: Manager correlation is set on the source, at the bottom of its Account Correlation page. The identity profile maps Manager Name, but the attributes to compare are chosen on the source.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to correlate managers on the custom identity attribute workerId, but it does not appear in the Identity Attribute list. What should the engineer do?
choices: Rename workerId to identificationNumber in every identity profile's mappings
Mark workerId as searchable with the identity attribute API
Add workerId to the HR source's entitlement schema
Create a search query that returns the workerId values
questions.answer: Mark workerId as searchable with the identity attribute API
questions.explanation: Custom attributes must be marked searchable through the identity attribute API to be used in manager correlation, and up to six can be used. This flag is unrelated to the Search feature.

questions.stem: Each employee's manager is identified by combining a country code field and a local ID field, and no single attribute holds the full value. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Configure two manager correlation sections on the source
Map Manager Name to the country code field only
Assign managers by hand on each identity's details page after every aggregation
Use a manager correlation rule to define the matching logic
questions.answer: Use a manager correlation rule to define the matching logic
questions.explanation: When matching is more complex than a single attribute comparison, a manager correlation rule supplies the logic. A source has one manager correlation configuration, and manual assignment does not scale.

questions.stem: HR changes an employee's manager field to an ID that matches no identity in the tenant. What happens to the employee's manager?
choices: The employee's manager is cleared to null
The employee is correlated to the source owner
The employee stays correlated to the existing manager
The employee is flagged with an identity exception
questions.answer: The employee stays correlated to the existing manager
questions.explanation: When the account value changes to something that cannot be correlated, the identity keeps its existing manager. Only a change to null clears the manager.

questions.stem: An identity has accounts on the Employees source, whose profile has priority 10, and the Contractors source, priority 20. Both sources have manager correlation, but the employee record's manager field is empty. Which source's value is used for manager correlation?
choices: The contractor source, the first in priority order with a non-null value
The employee source, because the higher priority profile always wins for manager data
Neither source, because priority 10 has an empty value
The source aggregated most recently, whatever its priority
questions.answer: The contractor source, the first in priority order with a non-null value
questions.explanation: Profiles are evaluated in priority order for manager correlation, and the first source with a non-null manager value is used. An empty value on the higher priority source does not stop the check.

questions.stem: An engineer adds a custom identity attribute named badgeNumber while editing the Employees profile. What happens in the Contractors profile?
choices: The attribute appears there too but can stay unmapped
The attribute is hidden until the engineer adds it again
The attribute is mapped automatically to the same source
Contractor identities fail processing until it is mapped
questions.answer: The attribute appears there too but can stay unmapped
questions.explanation: Custom identity attributes are tenant-wide, so they appear in every profile, but each profile can choose whether to map them. Unmapped attributes do not cause errors.

questions.stem: The union code from HR must appear on each identity's details page and be used in access request segments. It is not an identity attribute today. What should the engineer do?
choices: Reference the HR account attribute directly in each segment's identity criteria
Store the union code in the department attribute
Ask SailPoint Support to add the attribute to the tenant
Add a custom identity attribute, map it to the HR union code and apply changes
questions.answer: Add a custom identity attribute, map it to the HR union code and apply changes
questions.explanation: Adding and mapping a custom identity attribute makes the value available to role criteria and other features. Overloading a default attribute breaks its meaning, and support is not needed.

questions.stem: An engineer types Hire Date as the name of a new identity attribute. What happens to the technical name?
choices: It must be typed by hand and must start with an underscore
It is copied from the HR source attribute selected later
It populates automatically as a camel case version of the name
It is generated as a random string that cannot be changed
questions.answer: It populates automatically as a camel case version of the name
questions.explanation: The Technical Name fills in automatically in camel case from the Name, for example hireDate. The Name field itself accepts only letters, numbers and spaces.

questions.stem: Before deleting a custom identity attribute named region, which check is MOST important?
choices: Confirm that the region attribute has no value left in the HR source records
Find roles, transforms, rules and lifecycle logic that use it
Confirm that region is mapped in only one profile
Confirm that no certification is currently active
questions.answer: Find roles, transforms, rules and lifecycle logic that use it
questions.explanation: Deleting a custom attribute removes it from every profile and can break roles, transforms, rules, SAML attribute maps and lifecycle calculations that use it. Its mapping in one profile does not limit the impact.

questions.stem: An engineer deletes a custom identity attribute that was mapped only in the Employees profile. What must the engineer do afterwards?
choices: Run identity processing only on the Employees profile
Re-aggregate every source in the tenant
Run identity processing on each identity profile in the list
Recreate the attribute in the other profiles
questions.answer: Run identity processing on each identity profile in the list
questions.explanation: After deleting a custom attribute, identity processing must be run on each identity profile, even where the attribute was not mapped. Aggregation does not replace that step.

questions.stem: An engineer needs a custom identity attribute named Cost Center Region. Which name rule applies in the Add New Attribute dialog?
choices: The name must be entered in camel case
The name can contain only letters, numbers and spaces
The name must end with the source name
The name can contain any special character
questions.answer: The name can contain only letters, numbers and spaces
questions.explanation: The Name field accepts letters, numbers and spaces, and the Technical Name is generated in camel case from it. Special characters are not allowed.

questions.stem: An engineer needs to calculate a displayName value from HR data. Both a transform and an Identity Attribute rule could do it. Which approach is BEST practice?
choices: Use the rule, because rules always run faster than transforms
Use the rule, because transforms cannot read the account attributes of other sources
Use both, so the rule can check the transform's output
Use a transform, because rules need SailPoint review and add maintenance
questions.answer: Use a transform, because rules need SailPoint review and add maintenance
questions.explanation: Transforms are configuration the tenant team owns, while rules must be reviewed by SailPoint before deployment. Rules are kept for logic that transforms cannot express.

questions.stem: How does an engineer select an Identity Attribute rule for an identity attribute in the identity profile mappings?
choices: Choose Complex Data Source, then pick the rule from the Transform list
Choose the HR source, then type the rule's name into the Attribute dropdown list
Attach the rule to the HR source's correlation configuration
Upload the rule on the identity profile's Settings page
questions.answer: Choose Complex Data Source, then pick the rule from the Transform list
questions.explanation: Rules are applied to an identity attribute by selecting Complex Data Source and then the rule. Correlation and source settings do not populate identity attributes.

questions.stem: Which rule type is used to calculate an identity attribute's value in an identity profile mapping?
choices: Correlation rule
Identity Attribute rule
Before Provisioning rule
Build Map rule
questions.answer: Identity Attribute rule
questions.explanation: The Identity Attribute rule is a cloud rule that returns an identity attribute value. Correlation rules link accounts, Before Provisioning rules change provisioning plans and Build Map rules shape delimited or JDBC data.

questions.stem: An engineer has written a new Identity Attribute rule. How does it become available in the tenant?
choices: It is uploaded by the engineer with the transforms API
It is placed on the virtual appliance and picked up at the next service restart
It is submitted to SailPoint for review and deployed after approval
It is pasted into the identity profile's mapping editor
questions.answer: It is submitted to SailPoint for review and deployed after approval
questions.explanation: Cloud rules such as Identity Attribute rules run in SailPoint's cloud and must pass SailPoint's review before deployment. Transforms can be uploaded through the API, but rules cannot.

questions.stem: An engineer created a custom transform with the transforms API. How is it applied to an identity attribute?
choices: Choose Complex Data Source, then choose the transform from the rule list
Attach the transform to the source's account schema attribute
Reference the transform from the identity profile's priority setting
Pick the source and attribute, then choose it from the Transform list
questions.answer: Pick the source and attribute, then choose it from the Transform list
questions.explanation: Uploaded transforms appear in the Transform list of the identity profile mapping beside the built-in simple transforms. Complex Data Source is for rules.

questions.stem: The displayName identity attribute must read Last, First from two HR attributes. Which approach is the MOST direct?
choices: A concat transform that joins the two HR attributes with a separator
An Identity Attribute rule that reads both attributes
Two mappings to displayName, one for each attribute
A lookup transform that maps each employee's first name to their last name
questions.answer: A concat transform that joins the two HR attributes with a separator
questions.explanation: concat joins several values, including account attribute references and static text such as a comma, without a rule. An attribute has only one mapping, and lookup is for value tables.

questions.stem: Match each manager correlation item to its role.

pairs.match: Value examined on the manager's identity
Employee's account attribute that names the manager
Identity profile setting that must exist for managers to appear
Logic for matching that a single field comparison cannot handle
Lets a custom identity attribute be used for matching

targets_extra: Grants the manager an access profile at hire
questions.explanation: Manager correlation compares an account attribute with an identity attribute on the manager, needs Manager Name mapped, and uses a rule or searchable custom attributes when needed.

questions.stem: An engineer is building the minimum mapping for a new contractor identity profile. Which TWO attributes, besides User Name, must be mapped?
choices: Work Email
Last Name
Manager Name
Department
Lifecycle State
questions.explanation: User Name, Work Email and Last Name are required in every profile. Manager Name and Lifecycle State are needed only for features that rely on them.

questions.stem: Employees and contractors are in separate identity profiles, and the business wants different termination behaviour for each group. Which design is valid?
choices: Define a terminated state in each identity profile with its own actions
Define one tenant-wide terminated state that both identity profiles share
Define the terminated state only in the higher priority profile
Define termination actions on each source instead of in states
questions.answer: Define a terminated state in each identity profile with its own actions
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states are defined per identity profile, so each profile can have its own terminated state and actions. There is no tenant-wide lifecycle state.

questions.stem: An engineer creates a new lifecycle state named Sabbatical and maps identities to its technical name, but no identities enter the state. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The identity profile has a priority of 10
The state has no access profiles assigned
The state name contains an uppercase letter
The lifecycle state has not been enabled
questions.answer: The lifecycle state has not been enabled
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states are disabled by default and must be enabled before identities are assigned to them. A state with no access profiles is still valid.

questions.stem: An identity's Lifecycle State attribute holds the value Active, and the profile's state has the technical name active. The identity shows a status message instead of a state. Which status is it?
choices: Lifecycle State Not Set
Lifecycle State Does Not Match Technical Name Case
Lifecycle State Not Valid
Lifecycle State Pending Approval
questions.answer: Lifecycle State Does Not Match Technical Name Case
questions.explanation: The comparison with technical names is case-sensitive, so Active does not match active and the case-mismatch status appears. Not Set means the value is null or unmapped.

questions.stem: Department-specific birthright access differs across 40 departments, while all active employees get the same email and VPN access. Which design is BEST?
choices: Create one lifecycle state per department, each granting its own access profiles
Grant every department's access profiles in the active state
Grant common access in the active state and use department roles for the rest
Have managers request department access for each new hire
questions.answer: Grant common access in the active state and use department roles for the rest
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states suit access that depends on employment status, while roles with membership criteria scale for attribute-based access. Forty department states would multiply the lifecycle logic.

questions.stem: Which lifecycle states does Identity Security Cloud include automatically for a newly created identity profile?
choices: Active and inactive only
Joiner, mover and leaver
Pre-hire, active, leave of absence, terminated and archived
Pending, approved and revoked
questions.answer: Pre-hire, active, leave of absence, terminated and archived
questions.explanation: New identity profiles include pre-hire, active, leave of absence, terminated and archived states, and more can be added. Joiner, mover and leaver are process names, not states.

questions.stem: How many lifecycle states can an identity be assigned at the same time?
choices: One per authoritative source the identity has
One per role the identity is a member of
As many as its cloudLifecycleState values list
One lifecycle state at a time
questions.answer: One lifecycle state at a time
questions.explanation: An identity is in exactly one lifecycle state, set by its Lifecycle State attribute or by a manual change. Sources and roles do not add states.

questions.stem: An identity shows the status Lifecycle State Not Valid. What does this indicate?
choices: Its Lifecycle State attribute is not mapped in the identity profile at all
Its value matches none of the states defined in its identity profile
Its lifecycle state is enabled but has no actions
Its lifecycle state was changed by an admin by hand
questions.answer: Its value matches none of the states defined in its identity profile
questions.explanation: Not Valid means the attribute holds a value that is not a technical name of the profile's states. An unmapped or null value shows Not Set instead.

questions.stem: Identities are created from HR in a pre-hire state two weeks before their start date. The company wants them invited to Identity Security Cloud only on day one. What should the engineer configure?
choices: Automatic invitations when identities enter the active state
Manual invitations sent by the manager on day one
An invitation sent when the HR source is aggregated
An invitation sent automatically when the identity enters the pre-hire state
questions.answer: Automatic invitations when identities enter the active state
questions.explanation: Identity profiles can send invitations automatically when identities enter a chosen lifecycle state, such as active on the start date. Inviting at pre-hire or aggregation would be too early.

questions.stem: The lifecycle state must change from prehire to active on the start date even when HR sends no update that day. Which mapping design supports this?
choices: A date-comparison transform on startDate marked requiresPeriodicRefresh
A static transform that always returns active
A lookup transform on the HR employee status code that HR updates on day one
A manual lifecycle change by HR on each start date
questions.answer: A date-comparison transform on startDate marked requiresPeriodicRefresh
questions.explanation: A transform that compares startDate with the current date must be tagged requiresPeriodicRefresh so scheduled processing recalculates it daily. Without that, the value only changes when the identity's data changes.

questions.stem: A rehired employee returns to the active state, but the old Active Directory account that was disabled at termination stays disabled. What should the engineer change?
choices: Configure the terminated state to delete accounts instead of disabling them
Add the AD source to the active state's excluded sources
Ask the employee to request a new AD account
Configure the active state to enable accounts on the relevant sources
questions.answer: Configure the active state to enable accounts on the relevant sources
questions.explanation: The active state needs an enable accounts action for sources whose accounts were disabled at termination. Deleting at termination would remove history and is a separate design choice.

questions.stem: Managers want an email when a new hire becomes active. Where should the engineer configure this?
choices: In the HR source's Account Correlation settings, under Manager Correlation
In the active state's Email Notification List, selecting Manager
In the Approval Settings reminders section
In the identity profile's Mappings page
questions.answer: In the active state's Email Notification List, selecting Manager
questions.explanation: Each lifecycle state has an Email Notification List that can notify the manager, all SailPoint admins or specific addresses. Approval reminders relate to pending access requests.

questions.stem: New hires need a mailbox ready before their first day, but must not get VPN until they start. Which design meets this?
choices: Grant both access profiles in pre-hire and disable the VPN account until day one
Grant both access profiles in active on the start date
Grant the mailbox in pre-hire and the VPN access profile in active
Grant the VPN access profile in pre-hire and remove it at active
questions.answer: Grant the mailbox in pre-hire and the VPN access profile in active
questions.explanation: Each lifecycle state grants its own access profiles, so splitting them between pre-hire and active matches the timing. Granting everything at once misses either the early mailbox or the VPN control.

questions.stem: Which identity state is appropriate for a pre-hire lifecycle state?
choices: Active, because the identity is joining the organization
Inactive (long-term), because the person has not started
Inactive (short-term), because the person is not working yet
No identity state, because pre-hire identities are hidden
questions.answer: Active, because the identity is joining the organization
questions.explanation: The Active identity state covers people who are joining or working for the organization. Inactive (long-term) is for people who have separated and removes them from most services.

questions.stem: An engineer enables Remove all access on the terminated state. Which access does a terminated identity keep?
choices: All access that was approved through an access request
Birthright role access and access profiles granted by the terminated state
All access profiles that were granted by the identity's previous lifecycle state
Entitlements on sources with no disable action
questions.answer: Birthright role access and access profiles granted by the terminated state
questions.explanation: Remove all access revokes roles, access profiles and entitlements, but keeps birthright role access and access profiles granted by the current state. Requested access is removed, and approvals for removal are bypassed.

questions.stem: The terminated state disables accounts on All sources. Six months later a new SaaS source is onboarded. What happens when an identity is terminated after that?
choices: Accounts on the new source stay enabled until the source is added to the list by hand
The terminated state stops working until it is saved again
Accounts on the new source are deleted instead of disabled
Accounts on the new source are disabled too, unless the source is excluded
questions.answer: Accounts on the new source are disabled too, unless the source is excluded
questions.explanation: With All sources selected, newly created sources are included automatically, and sources can be excluded. This makes All sources a low-maintenance leaver design.

questions.stem: The archived state should delete accounts on specific sources 90 days after termination. The Delete Accounts option is unavailable. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The state is configured to remove all access
The state has an email notification configured
The state's identity state is not set to Inactive (long-term)
The archived state is not the highest priority state
questions.answer: The state's identity state is not set to Inactive (long-term)
questions.explanation: Delete operations can only be configured when the identity state is Inactive (long-term), and they are not available with All sources. Remove all access and notifications do not block deletion.

questions.stem: The archived state deletes Active Directory accounts, but some deleted accounts reappear after the next identity refresh. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The AD source's deletion threshold was exceeded
The identities still have a role that includes AD entitlements
The archived state does not send email notifications
The AD accounts were disabled first, which blocks a later delete operation
questions.answer: The identities still have a role that includes AD entitlements
questions.explanation: An active role assignment provisions its entitlements again, recreating the deleted account. Roles should be removed before accounts are deleted.

questions.stem: Legal requires that a leaver's mailbox stay active for 30 days so the manager can review it, while all other access ends on the termination date. Which design meets this?
choices: A terminated state that deletes all accounts, including email
A terminated state that keeps all accounts enabled for 30 days, then disables everything
A manual task asking IT to disable email each month
Terminate by disabling all sources except email, then disable email in a later state
questions.answer: Terminate by disabling all sources except email, then disable email in a later state
questions.explanation: Two states give two timings: termination disables everything except the mailbox, and a post-termination state based on the end date handles email. The other designs either lose the mailbox or keep everything active.

questions.stem: The terminated state disables Active Directory and also grants an access profile that moves accounts to a Disabled Users OU. Terminated users' AD accounts stay enabled. Why?
choices: Accounts are not disabled on a source the state also grants an access profile on
Access profiles granted in a terminated state are ignored by the provisioning engine
AD accounts can only be disabled by a workflow
The Disabled Users OU blocks the disable operation
questions.answer: Accounts are not disabled on a source the state also grants an access profile on
questions.explanation: Source accounts are not disabled or deleted if the state also grants an access profile on that source. The OU move belongs elsewhere, for example in a Before Provisioning rule on the disable operation.

questions.stem: A leave of absence state should mark people as away so they cannot be selected in the Request Center, while scheduled processing and attribute sync still apply to them. Which identity state fits BEST?
choices: Inactive (long-term)
Active
Inactive (short-term)
Archived
questions.answer: Inactive (short-term)
questions.explanation: Inactive (short-term) is meant for leave or separation in progress and still receives scheduled processing and attribute sync, while only Active identities can be selected in the Request Center. Long-term removes the identity from most services, and Archived is a lifecycle state, not an identity state.

questions.stem: Which kind of access item can be granted directly in a lifecycle state's configuration?
choices: Roles
Individual entitlements
Access profiles
Applications
questions.answer: Access profiles
questions.explanation: A lifecycle state's Access Profiles tab grants access profiles; roles are assigned through membership criteria. Individual entitlements must be wrapped in an access profile.

questions.stem: An identity moves from the contractor-active state to the terminated state. Both grant the Badge Access access profile, and only contractor-active grants VPN. What happens?
choices: Both access profiles are revoked
Both access profiles are kept
Badge Access is revoked and VPN is kept
VPN is revoked and Badge Access is kept
questions.answer: VPN is revoked and Badge Access is kept
questions.explanation: Access profiles granted by a lifecycle state are revoked when the identity leaves it, unless the new state also grants them. Badge Access is in both states, so it stays.

questions.stem: A helpdesk analyst removes an access profile from an active employee, and the access profile is granted by the active lifecycle state. What happens next?
choices: The access profile stays removed until the next certification campaign is completed
The access profile is provisioned again while the identity stays in that state
The identity's lifecycle state changes to manual
The access profile is removed from the lifecycle state too
questions.answer: The access profile is provisioned again while the identity stays in that state
questions.explanation: Lifecycle state access profiles are enforced while the identity remains in the state, so removing one leads to it being provisioned again. Change the state configuration or the identity's state instead.

questions.stem: A disable action in the terminated state failed for one account because the target system was offline for two days. What should the engineer know about retries?
choices: Retryable errors are retried hourly up to three times, then need follow-up
The action retries every hour until the account is disabled
The action runs again at every identity refresh until the account is finally disabled
Failed lifecycle actions are always ignored and never retried
questions.answer: Retryable errors are retried hourly up to three times, then need follow-up
questions.explanation: Lifecycle actions run once and are not a persistent enforcement mechanism; retryable errors are retried once an hour up to three times. After a long outage, the engineer must confirm and fix the account.

questions.stem: An engineer configures the terminated state to disable accounts on the ERP source and also tries to delete accounts on the same ERP source in that state. What is the result?
choices: The account is disabled first, then deleted
The account is deleted, and the disable is skipped
The account is disabled at once, and the deletion waits for the archived state
It is not allowed, because a source can have only one operation per state
questions.answer: It is not allowed, because a source can have only one operation per state
questions.explanation: Each source can be configured for only one operation per lifecycle state. Disabling and then deleting needs two states, such as terminated and archived.

questions.stem: Which recipients can an engineer choose in a lifecycle state's Email Notification List?
choices: The identity's governance groups and source owners
The manager, all SailPoint admins and specific email addresses
The access profile owners of the state's access profiles
The requesters of the identity's open access requests
questions.answer: The manager, all SailPoint admins and specific email addresses
questions.explanation: Lifecycle state notifications can go to the manager, all SailPoint admins or specific users by address, using the Lifecycle State Change email template. Owners and groups are not options.

questions.stem: HR sends status codes A, L and T, but the lifecycle states have technical names active, leaveOfAbsence and terminated. Which design calculates the Lifecycle State attribute BEST?
choices: A lookup transform that maps each HR code to a technical name
A ToUpper transform on the HR status code
Renaming the lifecycle states to A, L and T
A manual lifecycle change by an admin for each identity whenever HR status changes
questions.answer: A lookup transform that maps each HR code to a technical name
questions.explanation: A lookup transform converts source values into the exact technical names, with a default for unknown codes. Renaming states to codes makes them harder to read and does not handle bad values.

questions.stem: HR reports an urgent termination at 10 a.m., but the HR feed will not show it until the next day. What is the fastest way to start the leaver actions?
choices: Run a full aggregation of every connected source, then run identity processing
Delete the identity from the tenant
Manually set the identity's lifecycle state to terminated
Remove the identity from all of its roles
questions.answer: Manually set the identity's lifecycle state to terminated
questions.explanation: A manual lifecycle state change starts the state's provisioning at once and shows as Manual. Deleting the identity does not deprovision its accounts.

questions.stem: An admin manually set an identity to inactive. Later the HR status changes from active to leave of absence. What lifecycle state does the identity show?
choices: The manual inactive state, until an admin changes it
The automatic value calculated from the new HR data
No state, until the admin confirms the change
Both states, with the manual one taking effect
questions.answer: The automatic value calculated from the new HR data
questions.explanation: A manual setting holds only until the underlying source value changes, then the automatic value applies again. This prevents a manual state from hiding a real HR change forever.

questions.stem: When a leaver enters the terminated state, the company also wants a ticket opened in a service desk and a message to the security team. What should the engineer recommend?
choices: A workflow triggered when the identity's lifecycle state changes
A second email notification list on the terminated state that includes the service desk
An access profile that opens the ticket when it is removed
A certification campaign that runs each time an identity leaves
questions.answer: A workflow triggered when the identity's lifecycle state changes
questions.explanation: Workflows can listen for identity attribute changes such as cloudLifecycleState and run extra actions, including calls to external systems. Lifecycle states only manage accounts, access profiles and notifications.

questions.stem: The lifecycle state calculation needs the HR status, the start date and the end date together. Which approach should the engineer try FIRST?
choices: An Identity Attribute rule submitted for review
A separate lifecycle state for every combination of status, start date and end date
A combined transform using date comparison and conditional logic
A daily manual update by the HR team
questions.answer: A combined transform using date comparison and conditional logic
questions.explanation: Transforms can combine date comparisons, conditions and lookups without a rule. A rule is the fallback for logic transforms cannot express because it needs SailPoint review.

questions.stem: When are lifecycle states recalculated and their provisioning actions carried out?
choices: Only when an admin selects Apply Changes
Only during the nightly certification job
Only when the identity signs in to the tenant
During event-driven and scheduled identity processing
questions.answer: During event-driven and scheduled identity processing
questions.explanation: Lifecycle state changes are calculated as part of identity processing, which runs on data changes and on a schedule. Apply Changes is one way to start processing, not the only one.

questions.stem: An engineer is adding automatic lifecycle state assignment to an identity profile. Put the steps in order.
items: Create the lifecycle states and note their technical names
Configure each state's actions and enable it
Map the Lifecycle State attribute with a transform that returns technical names
Preview identities to confirm the calculated states
Apply changes to process the profile's identities
questions.explanation: States and technical names must exist before the attribute can be mapped to them, and Preview checks the calculation before Apply Changes starts processing and provisioning.

questions.stem: Match each lifecycle requirement to the lifecycle state setting that meets it.

pairs.item: Revoke requested access when someone leaves
Remove accounts after the retention period
Tell the manager when the state changes
Give every new hire a mailbox
Turn accounts back on for a rehire

questions.explanation: Each lifecycle state requirement maps to a specific state setting; manager correlation is an identity attribute setting, not a lifecycle state action.

questions.stem: Which TWO actions can a lifecycle state perform on its own?
choices: Disable accounts on selected sources
Grant access profiles to the identity
Assign roles directly to the identity
Open a service desk ticket
Launch a certification campaign
answers: Grant access profiles to the identity
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states enable, disable or delete accounts, remove access, grant access profiles and send notifications. Roles, tickets and campaigns need other features such as criteria and workflows.
